label: early original-phase token bigram detector (steps 1-2, input in {a,c,d,q,y,0} after q/f/a/e/y/c/1/x/o/3)
explanation: About 76% of activation mass is in the original phase, almost entirely at t=1 (52%) and t=2 (21%). It never fires at t=0, at the delimiter, or at original positions 4 and later. In that window it acts like a token-pair detector: the current input is one of d, a, c, q, y, 0 (d and a are strongest) and the previous token is one of q, f, a, e, y, c, 1, x, o, 3. The largest activations are o q d, o q a and 3 q d. The other ~24% of mass is spread thinly over the copy phase (recall_idx 2-6), mostly on steps whose output is o, z or 3. That part is imprecise (about 7-12%) and is not captured. On dev the predicate has F1 0.47 and mass recall 0.56; adding the copy-phase clause raised recall but cut precision a lot. I did not check magnitude beyond the token rankings above.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the second original token (most: d, a, c, y, q, 0; least: w, 2, n, z) and the previous input (most: q, f, e, 1, x, a; least: z, s, <DEL>, -); timing cues that raise it most: t=1, t=2, L=3 & t=4.
